# Agent capability matrix

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-agent-capability-matrix.mjs from
     docs/reference/agents/capability-matrix.source.json, cross-checked against the code
     registries. Do not edit by hand; run `npm run docs:agents:generate`. -->

Current stable release: **v1.5.0**. Status vocabulary is defined in [terminology](../terminology.md):

- `stable` — in the current stable download;
- `main` — implemented on `main`, not yet in a stable release;
- `legacy` — detect-only terminal entry, no managed conversation;
- `fixture-qualified` — automated fixture suites pass; no recorded real-CLI run on any platform;
- `live-qualified: <os>` — a real-CLI run is recorded for the listed operating systems only.

Three verbs are kept apart throughout: **upstream supports** (the CLI itself can do it), **VaneHub manages** (VaneHub writes or drives it), **VaneHub verifies** (a recorded test proves it). "VaneHub does not manage X" never means "upstream does not support X".

## Permission projection notes

A policy template (`readonly`, `standard`, `trusted`, `yolo`) is enforced at the host decision point for every agent. What the CLI process is launched with is a separate projection and differs by transport; `trusted` and `yolo` project identically except on Qwen Code, Kimi Code CLI, and iFlow CLI terminals. Per-template flags are tabulated in the developer guide's [permission model](../../developer-guide/src/permission-model.md).

| Agent | Enforceability |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Launch sets `--permission-mode`; the PreToolUse hook is the action-level boundary. Host-projected. |
| Codex CLI | `--sandbox` and `--ask-for-approval` per template. Host-projected. |
| OpenCode | `--agent plan` / `OPENCODE_PERMISSION` env / `--auto`. Host-projected. |
| Antigravity CLI | `--mode plan\|accept-edits` and `--sandbox`; never `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Host-projected. |
| Gemini CLI | `--approval-mode plan\|default\|yolo`. Host-projected. |
| Qwen Code | PTY: `--approval-mode plan\|default\|auto-edit\|yolo`; ACP: only the read-only flag, other templates answered per call by the host. Host-projected. |
| Kimi Code CLI | PTY: `--plan` / CLI default / `--yolo` / `--auto`; ACP: only the read-only flag. Host-projected. |
| Qoder CLI | No plan/read-only mode upstream: a read-only terminal launch is refused (`terminal-readonly-unsupported`). PTY: `--permission-mode default\|accept_edits`; ACP: no flag. |
| CodeBuddy Code | PTY: `--permission-mode plan\|default\|acceptEdits`; ACP: only the read-only flag. Host-projected. |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | PTY: `--mode plan` / no flag on standard (provider-delegated ask-first) / `--allow-all-tools`; ACP: only the read-only flag. |
| Cursor Agent CLI | PTY: `--mode plan` / no flag on standard (provider-delegated ask-first) / `--force`; ACP: only the read-only flag. Binary is identity-checked, not matched by name. |
| iFlow CLI | PTY only: `--plan\|--default\|--autoEdit\|--yolo`. Official service ended 2026-04-17; no managed conversation. |
| OnePiece | Every tool call goes through the unified decision point directly; nothing to project. |

## Provider configuration notes

`exclusive` — VaneHub writes one active profile into the CLI's own configuration file and restores the previous values on switch; `additive` — VaneHub adds its entry beside existing ones (OpenCode); `apply-only` — VaneHub applies model/approval fields but manages no endpoint or credential field; `not-applicable` — the CLI exposes no third-party endpoint VaneHub could manage; `native-catalog` — OnePiece's own provider catalog.

| Agent | Managed file | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/settings.json` | — |
| Codex CLI | `~/.codex/config.toml + auth.json` | — |
| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | — |
| Antigravity CLI | `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` | VaneHub applies model and approval fields but manages no endpoint or credential field; the upstream CLI itself supports API keys and compatible endpoints. |
| Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/.env` | — |
| Qwen Code | `~/.qwen/.env + settings.json` | — |
| Kimi Code CLI | — | — |
| Qoder CLI | — | — |
| CodeBuddy Code | — | — |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | — | — |
| Cursor Agent CLI | — | — |
| iFlow CLI | `~/.iflow/settings.json` | — |
| OnePiece | — | 25-provider catalog or a custom compatible endpoint; key stored in the OS credential service. |

## Auth probe notes

`signed-in` means VaneHub can read the CLI's own login status; `unknown` means only the version is probed and the settings page never starts a login. Vendor subscription login always happens in your terminal.

- **Claude Code** — Deliberately undocumented upstream; `claude doctor` is probed instead.
- **Codex CLI** — `codex login status`.
- **OpenCode** — `opencode auth list`.
- **OnePiece** — Credential presence only; the API key is validated once before saving.

## Evaluation notes

Candidates are every registered agent whose capability tags do not include `legacy`; available agents are preselected, at most eight per arena.

- **iFlow CLI** — excluded: Tagged legacy: no managed conversation for an arena attempt to drive.
